name: Avilés
title: Avilés Ship Gauging: UTM for Bulkers and Metal Carriers
description: Ultrasonic thickness gauging in Avilés for bulk carriers, metal and general cargo ships: hold frames, ballast tanks, deck plating and pre-docking readings.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement for Ships in the Ría de Avilés
intro: Avilés sits on a sheltered ría on the Asturian coast, and its quays exist to feed and empty a steelworks and a metal industry. Bulk carriers bring ore, coal and limestone; general cargo ships take away coil, plate and aluminium. Those cargoes are hard on holds and tank tops. Gauging technicians travel from India to the ship, so the work is planned around the vessel's discharge and the visa lead time rather than around any base here.
keywords: hull thickness gauging spain north coast

highlights.h: Holds that carry ore and coal
highlights.p: Abrasive cargo and heavy grabs wear tank tops, lower hold frames and hopper plating faster than the age of the ship suggests. We gauge those areas systematically while the holds are empty and safe to enter.
Coil, plate and ingot carriers load concentrated weights on decks and tank tops. Readings around stowage areas, hatch coamings and lashing points show where steel has thinned under repeated loading.
A bulker may be alongside only as long as the cargo programme needs. We agree a priority order of holds and tanks with the chief officer beforehand so the most useful readings come first.

port.h: The Ría de Avilés: an industrial estuary on the Asturian coast
p: The port of Avilés occupies the lower reaches of a ría, a drowned river valley, and the outer area at San Juan de Nieva close to the breakwaters. Ships enter between the outer moles and then work up a dredged channel with industrial quays on both banks. The Cantabrian Sea off this coast can be rough from autumn to spring, and a north-westerly swell can keep ships waiting outside for a suitable tide and sea state. Once inside, the ría is sheltered, which makes alongside gauging comparatively comfortable for the technicians once the ship has berthed.

Traffic follows local industry. A large integrated steelworks on the ría takes iron ore, coal, coke and fluxes by sea, and ships it out as coil and plate. A primary aluminium plant and a zinc works nearby have historically added their own raw materials and metal products, and the Autoridad Portuaria de Avilés also handles fertiliser, scrap, wood products and general cargo. Most vessels are handy and supramax bulk carriers, coasters, metal carriers and the occasional tanker for the industrial users, together with port tugs, pilot boats and dredgers working in the channel.

Gauging demand here is therefore mostly structural wear in cargo spaces rather than hull fouling or machinery questions. Bulk carriers are surveyed on the enhanced programme and the quay stay can be used to measure hold frames, tank tops and hopper tank boundaries that cannot be reached at sea. General cargo ships carrying steel products arrive with local denting and thinning that owners want quantified before a survey or sale. Because many ships call repeatedly on the same ore or coil rotation, owners also gauge for trend: the same plates on the same frames, read every time the ship comes back.

facilities.h: Where a ship can be gauged in and around Avilés
p: Most work is done alongside at the industrial quays once discharge has opened the holds. Bulk carriers at the ore and coal berths can be gauged hold by hold as the grabs clear each space, subject to the terminal's safety rules and the ship's enclosed-space entry procedure. General cargo and metal carriers at the multipurpose quays allow access to the tank top, the hatch coamings and the underside of the hatch covers between cargo operations. Scrap and fertiliser calls are shorter, so the programme is cut down to the spaces that matter most.

Avilés is not a large-drydock port. Ships needing a dock for steel renewal normally go to a larger yard elsewhere on the northern or Galician coast, and readings taken in Avilés become the starting steel list for that docking. Small repair yards and slipways on the ría deal with coasters, tugs and workboats, and a technician team can gauge there when a vessel is hauled out. Anchorage work outside the breakwaters depends on sea state and is arranged through the ship's agent with a launch, but it is rarely the first choice on this exposed coast.
list: Ore, coal and bulk quays serving the steelworks: hold frame, tank top and hopper tank gauging during and after discharge
Multipurpose and metal-products quays: deck, coaming and hatch cover gauging on coil, plate and aluminium carriers
San Juan de Nieva outer area: general cargo and fertiliser berths for shorter-stay structural readings
Small ship-repair yards and slipways on the ría: coasters, tugs and workboats hauled for repair
Anchorage off the breakwaters: pre-arrival gauging by launch when sea state allows
Larger yards on the northern coast: docking-stage gauging after steel lists are prepared in Avilés

context.h: Port state control and the steel-trade backdrop
p: Ships calling at Avilés are inspected under the Paris MoU regime, carried out in Spain by marine inspectors attached to the Capitanía Marítima under the Dirección General de la Marina Mercante. Older bulk carriers and small general cargo ships on tramp rotations are frequent subjects, and inspectors pay close attention to hull condition, hatch covers and the state of cargo holds. A recent set of thickness readings gives the master something solid to show if structural questions arise, and gives the owner a record that stands independently of the last class report.

The EU Ship Recycling Regulation requires ships calling at EU ports to carry an Inventory of Hazardous Materials, and some owners combine IHM verification work with a structural check when a ship is approaching the end of its trading life. Carbon rules now bite on bulk tonnage too, because EU ETS covers voyages between EU ports and part of those starting or ending outside, and FuelEU Maritime has followed. A ship that must justify a retrofit or a long-term employment on the steel trade often asks first what steel it still has, and a gauging report is where that answer starts.

jobs.p: Requests from Avilés are shaped by cargo wear and by owners running older tonnage on regular ore, coal or coil rotations. Most come from superintendents who know which holds worry them, so the first conversation is about the programme: which spaces, in what order, and what the ship's discharge window allows. Where cracking is likely at frame brackets or coaming corners, magnetic particle equipment travels with the team. Examples of work we see here include:
list: Hold frame and lower bracket gauging on a supramax carrying coal and ore, ahead of its special survey and measured against the class diminution limits.
Tank top plating and hopper tank readings on a handy bulker after a long run of abrasive cargo, grid-spaced so wear patterns are visible on the report.
Deck and hatch coaming gauging on a metal carrier whose decks take heavy coil loads, with magnetic particle testing at coaming corners.
Ballast tank readings on a coaster during a planned lay-by, producing a steel estimate for a docking at a yard along the coast.
Owner's condition gauging of an older general cargo ship being considered for purchase, covering holds, tank tops and main deck.

logistics: Technicians usually fly from India to a European hub and then to Asturias Airport, which lies a short distance from the port, with Bilbao as an alternative when connections suit. Terminal access is arranged by the ship's agent, who also books a launch for any anchorage work. Spain is in the Schengen area, so visas must be issued before travel, and the team plans around that lead time and the vessel's expected arrival, especially in winter when weather can move the berthing time.

faqs.q: Can holds on a bulk carrier be gauged while it discharges ore or coal in Avilés?
faqs.a: Yes, once a hold has been emptied and cleared for entry. We agree the order of holds with the chief officer, wait for the ship's enclosed-space permit, and gauge frames, tank tops and hopper tanks while the next hold is still being worked. Dusty cargoes slow access, so a longer discharge produces a fuller set of readings than a short call.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock in Avilés for steel renewal after gauging?
faqs.a: Not for large merchant ships. Avilés has smaller repair facilities on the ría for coasters and workboats, while bigger vessels normally dock at yards elsewhere on the northern or Galician coast. Gauging in Avilés is often used to prepare the steel list, so the yard can order plate and plan crop-and-renew work before the ship arrives.

faqs.q: Does winter swell on the Asturian coast affect gauging at the quay?
faqs.a: Inside the ría the quays are well sheltered, so alongside gauging proceeds normally once the ship is berthed. The weather mostly affects arrival times, and a ship may wait outside for sea state. We keep technician travel flexible for this reason and adjust the schedule when the ship's agent reports a revised berthing time.

faqs.q: What is measured on general cargo ships that carry coil and plate?
faqs.a: The areas where concentrated loads act: tank top plating under stowage, hatch coaming tops and corners, the hatch cover skirts and the main deck around lashing points. Magnetic particle testing is added where cracks are suspected. The report records readings by plate or frame so that wear can be compared with earlier survey figures.

faqs.q: How early should a request for gauging in Avilés be sent?
faqs.a: As soon as the ship's schedule is known. Technicians need Schengen visas, and the measurement plan depends on which holds are being discharged and when. Short-notice requests are still worth sending with the berth, expected dates and scope, and we will tell you plainly whether a team can reach the ship in time.
